name: Aster Place
award: 2024 Federal 9% and state housing tax credits (Round One)
headline: Lincoln Avenue Communities, with the Garfield County Housing Authority as special limited partner, is developing Aster Place, a 58-unit all-electric family rental on Stone Quarry Road in the Battlement Mesa PUD (Parachute address) for households at 30% to 80% AMI, which won a 2024 Round One 9% and state credit award.
why_it_matters: It would be the first tax credit family rental in the Parachute and Battlement Mesa area, and it shows a rural deal stacking a housing authority partnership (property tax exemption and 8 project-based vouchers), a DOH soft loan and a CHFA SMART permanent loan with a rate buy-down to grow from 40 to 58 units.

status.label: Pre-leasing advertised for February 2027 move-ins; financing closing and construction start not confirmed
status.detail: In August 2025 Garfield County commissioners signed historic-preservation consultation letters that the developer called one of the last pieces needed to get a permit. A rental listing verified on 2026-10-21 advertises leasing for February 2027 move-ins. No dated public record of the financing closing, a building permit or a groundbreaking was found.

next_step: Watch for a Garfield County building permit for 5 Stone Quarry Road and a recorded CHFA land use restriction agreement, which would confirm closing; then lease-up ahead of the advertised February 2027 move-ins.

key_numbers.meaning: 14 one-, 28 two- and 16 three-bedroom units; 8 units at 30% AMI backed by project-based vouchers.

background.text: This was a resubmission: the prior year's application was for 40 units. The applicant says the DOH loan, tax exemption, income averaging, solar credits and the CHFA rate buy-down let it add 18 units and stay feasible.

Market case: the applicant's market study found 0.5% overall vacancy and 0.0% LIHTC vacancy in the market area, an 11% capture rate, and no new family LIHTC project completed in the market area since 2008; the nearest tax credit properties are in Rifle, about 19 miles away.

The application proposed no public outreach because the site is zoned for the use and needs only building permit review; it planned to submit plans to Garfield County in September 2024 and start construction in March 2025.
The Phase I found no recognized environmental conditions; it flagged a business environmental risk around excavated soils and recommended radon mitigation, which the applicant priced in.

In August 2025 Garfield County commissioners unanimously signed 10 letters to the State Historic Preservation Office and the Tribal Historic Preservation Officer as part of the project's environmental assessment, confirming no effect on archaeological or historic resources. The Post Independent reported the housing authority expects to allocate eight project-based vouchers.
The schedule has slipped: in October 2024 the housing authority estimated completion by early 2026; the current listing advertises February 2027 move-ins.
Application rents ranged from $744 (40% AMI one-bedroom) to $2,382 (30% AMI subsidized three-bedroom, contract rent with voucher). The current listing shows rents from $856 to $2,374.

discrepancies.text: CHFA's award report places the project in Battlement Mesa, while CHFA's applicant report and the application narrative give the city as Parachute.
The application describes two three-story buildings with 95 surface parking spaces, while the Post Independent describes one two-story and one three-story building with a 97-space lot.
The application gives unit sizes of 800, 1,100 and 1,250 sq ft for one-, two- and three-bedroom units, while the current rental listing shows 850, 1,150 and 1,300 sq ft.

open_questions: Whether the financing has closed and a Garfield County building permit has been issued; no dated record of either, or of a groundbreaking, was found.

Current property manager (the 2024 application named Shelton Residential / Asset Living; the listing does not name one in its text).
